one_sentence: This document establishes a registry of structural isomorphism records documenting cross-domain mappings between physics, theology, and other domains within the Theophysics framework.
executive_summary: The Isomorphism Registry (README) serves as the master index for all structural isomorphism records (ISO-001 through ISO-036) in the Theophysics Research Initiative. It defines the purpose, evaluation protocol, and maintenance rules for these records. Each ISO documents a claimed structural correspondence between two domains, evaluated against the Four-Test Protocol: Prediction Constraint, Symmetric Breaking, Connection Density, and Falsifiability Invitation. The registry includes a table of current records with domains, status, confidence, and type classifications, ranging from high-confidence structural isomorphisms (e.g., Math/Physics ↔ Trinity, Immunology ↔ Soteriology) to low-confidence analogies. The document concludes with instructions for adding new records and emphasizes that unfalsifiable isomorphisms are beliefs, not valid mappings.
short_summary: This document is the master README for the Isomorphism Registry, indexing all structural isomorphism records in the Theophysics framework. Its core structural claim is that each ISO record documents a cross-domain mapping evaluated against a four-test protocol. Key evidence includes a table of 36 current records with domains, statuses, and confidence levels. This matters because it provides the organizational backbone for the entire isomorphism research program, ensuring consistency, falsifiability, and honest classification.
